item.title: AI chip boom tripled South Korea's economic growth in the third quarter
item.description: South Korea's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter. However, analysts warned that its heavy reliance on the chip industry leaves the country vulnerable to a slowdown in global AI spending.

item.title: Macklemore begins Free Palestine tour in Europe with call for unity in Dublin
item.description: "I am proud to stand here on stage in solidarity with the Palestinian people. We will continue to fight for collective liberation until our last breath," Macklemore said on stage in Dublin last night.

item.title: Israelis head to polls in first general election since 7 October attacks with no clear favourite
item.description: With no party expected to win an outright majority, weeks of coalition talks could follow a vote being closely watched in European capitals.

item.title: Trump calls Norway a ‘shithouse country’ over Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description: US President Donald Trump has launched a fresh verbal attack on Norway, branding the Nordic nation a “shithouse country”.

item.title: Rogue AI, cyberattacks and weapons: the risks Anthropic is warning investors about ahead of its IPO
item.description: The AI company’s IPO paperwork warns of potential harms from increasingly autonomous systems, alongside financial and regulatory challenges.

item.title: Star Trek actor Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov, dies aged 90
item.description: Koenig's death leaves William Shatner, who played Capt. James T. Kirk, and George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu, as the only surviving members of the original series' main cast.

item.title: Merz courts Asian investors as he insists Europe remains a safe bet
item.description: The German chancellor's upbeat pitch comes at a time of mounting pressure in Berlin, where a ministerial resignation and rising far-right support have left the chancellor’s coalition on shaky ground.

item.title: Israel: October 7 families remember victims as voters head to polls
item.description: In Tel Aviv, families affected by the 7 October 2023 attacks observed a moment of silence as polling stations were opening across Israel for the general election.

item.title: EU Inc: Why the Commission's perfect startup plan might be falling apart
item.description: EU Inc, the Commission’s promise to strengthen the EU’s startup market and keep startups from moving abroad, is facing roadblocks that make its adoption by 2026 difficult. Will the 28th regime survive?

item.title: European natural gas prices soar: What it means for your winter bills
item.description: Gas prices have tripled in 2026 and EU storage is at a record low. Analysts explain what it means for winter bills and how long it could last.

item.title: A pivotal election in Israel, and Netanyahu’s next test
item.description: Good morning. It’s Tuesday, and this is what’s on today’s docket: Election fever spreads to Israel, Zelenskyy bemoans a lack of American Patriot missiles, and the European continent is only getting hotter, according to the EU climate chief. I’m Angela Skujins. Let’s dive in.

item.title: Harry Kane is first Bundesliga player since Matthias Sammer to win Ballon d'Or
item.description: The Bayern Munich striker's award ends a decades-long wait for a Bundesliga player or Englishman to receive the prestigious trophy.

item.title: Scientists uncover new clues to the actual night sky behind Van Gogh’s The Starry Night
item.description: Researchers led by South Korean scientist Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim argue that Vincent van Gogh's painting may show the Taurus constellation rather than Aries, challenging the accepted timeline of the impressionist masterpiece.

item.title: Europe Today: Israel votes on Netanyahu's future as Orbán is floated for UN chief
item.description: Israelis vote today in their first election since 7 October, with Benjamin Netanyahu's future on the line. Washington is reportedly floating Viktor Orbán for UN secretary-general. And we interview EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra to ask what Lula's re-election means for Europe.

item.title: London’s most famous shopping street is now pedestrianised
item.description: Ahead of the holiday season, cars, buses and bikes are banned from nearly a kilometre of Oxford Street.

item.title: Deadly parasite: How fox tapeworm warns of pandemic X
item.description: The WHO has developed an early warning system to spot looming pandemics. Tropical medicine expert Dr Carsten Köhler from Tübingen explains the background to Euronews.

item.title: Europe must prepare for a 3°C warmer world, EU climate chief warns
item.description: As Brussels warns that Europe must prepare for increasingly extreme weather, new EU rules will require governments to clarify who is responsible for climate preparedness – but no new funding is being offered to help households adapt.

item.title: Blood test could reveal prostate cancer risk more than a decade before diagnosis
item.description: Proteins present in men’s blood could give clues to prostate cancer risk years before diagnosis.

item.title: Dog scared of fireworks? Switzerland could bring in a nationwide ban if public votes yes
item.description: Fireworks were banned in the Netherlands earlier this year on safety and environmental grounds.

item.title: Dating costs in Europe: Which cities are cheapest and most expensive?
item.description: Dating can be costly across Europe. Some cities are incredibly expensive, but the picture changes when salaries are taken into account.

item.title: Seeking guaranteed snow? These are Europe’s most reliable ski resorts and regions
item.description: A new study has ranked Europe’s most reliable ski resorts and regions. Here are the top destinations to consider for your next active winter getaway.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 27th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Ukraine's €70 billion shortfall could make or break the next EU budget
item.description: Brussels faces a highly charged mix as the fight over the next EU budget overlaps with the efforts to plug Ukraine's €70 billion gap.

item.title: Spanish language learning surges in China but teachers are in short supply
item.description: Spanish language teaching is booming in China, with enrolments up 12.6% between 2023 and 2025. But the Cervantes Institute says there's a shortage of teachers to meet rising demand.

item.title: US-brokered ceasefire begins in Russian-occupied Oleshky as strikes hit Kyiv
item.description: Announcing last Friday that she had brokered the ceasefire, Melania Trump said civilian officials from both Russia and Ukraine would visit residents in their homes and "determine the level of assistance they require".

item.title: France: crowds fill Marseille's Old Port in anti-racism protest
item.description: Hundreds of people gathered at Marseille's Vieux-Port on Monday evening to protest against racism following a deadly shooting near Paris. Police estimated the crowd at 800, while organisers put attendance at more than 1,000.

item.title: Turkey-Libya maritime boundaries deal 'remains null and void,' Greek foreign minister says
item.description: The joint statement responded to the recent decision by Libya's House of Representatives to ratify the 2019 memorandum.

item.title: Trump says Brazil election looked 'rigged' without giving evidence
item.description: The Trump administration has hailed a recent wave of right-wing election victories across South America.

item.title: Microsoft offers around 60,000 employees voluntary buyouts
item.description: The offer will be made available to employees on select teams across the US, Canada, India and the United Kingdom "at level 70 and below," meaning some senior staff could be included. Around 60,000 employees are reported to be eligible.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows off soaring revenues as the company warns of AI's 'risks to humanity'
item.description: Anthropic warned AI could bring "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" if it is not "developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures."

item.title: María Corina Machado seeks talks with Delcy Rodríguez after return from exile
item.description: After a year in exile, Venezuela's opposition leader returns, ready to negotiate with the government. The EU welcomes her and calls for free and fair elections.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV confirms Latin America trip after recovering from surgery
item.description: The Vatican says the Pope is recovering well and will be able to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November, with doctors ruling out any complications that could derail the trip.

item.title: Russia: flames engulf buildings after Ukrainian drone attack in Voronezh region
item.description: At least two people were killed and 17 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Voronezh region. Flames engulfed buildings, while falling debris struck a commuter train.

item.title: Zelenskyy calls out monthlong wait for Hegseth to sign off on Patriot missiles
item.description: Kyiv has repeatedly pressed the need for more interceptors to be delivered to its forces as Ukraine continues to defend against deadly Russian missile attacks and jet-powered drone strikes.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 26th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: UK: Oxford Street pedestrianisation begins in central London
item.description: Pedestrians have taken over part of London's Oxford Street as a new traffic ban comes into force.

item.title: Exclusive: EU to give Frontex new powers to deport migrants from outside Europe
item.description: Under new rules, the EU border agency will be allowed to transfer migrants between third countries, expanding its operations beyond Europe and facilitating deportations from return hubs.

item.title: EU set to miss 2030 marine protection targets, auditors warn
item.description: Despite designating 14% of its waters as protected areas, the EU has placed less than 1% under strict protection, leaving marine ecosystems vulnerable to damaging fishing practices and putting its 2030 biodiversity targets at risk.

item.title: Dictionary.com reveals 2026 Word of the Year - and it's a depressing one
item.description: The internet slang term / suffix "Maxxing" has officially been selected by Dictionary.com as its 2026 Word of the Year.

item.title: Swedish government blocks ChatGPT and Claude. Here’s why
item.description: The ban on employees using browser-based versions of ChatGPT and Claude took effect on Monday 26 October amid security concerns over data processing.

item.title: Cyprus signs $1.8bn deal to develop first gas field, with exports to Europe via Egypt
item.description: The deal is a key step towards harnessing Cyprus' natural gas reserves and bolstering energy cooperation in the Eastern Mediterranean, with exports to Europe via Egypt and production due to start in 2028.

item.title: From the Mecca defence pact to Tehran talks: Is the Middle East’s security landscape shifting?
item.description: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are pursuing talks with Tehran while strengthening their military readiness under the terms of the Mecca Defence Alliance.

item.title: ‘Hybrid weapon of war’: Why climate disinformation could be a growing public health threat
item.description: “Climate disinformation is not only a problem of false rumours and mistruths; it is also a problem of power, incentives and accountability.”

item.title: 'Pure garbage': Elon Musk’s AI-generated 'The Odyssey' clip ridiculed online
item.description: The AI slop clip has been blasted online, with many calling it out as "garbage" and an "utter waste of time and money like most of Musk Inc."

item.title: Serbia’s student victory raises hopes of an EU reset
item.description: The Student List’s election win ends Vučić’s 14-year rule and raises hopes of an EU reset, but its stance on Russia sanctions and Kosovo leaves Brussels cautious.

item.title: First international flight arrives at the new Western Sydney airport
item.description: Sydney’s new 24-hour airport has welcomed its first international passengers with the opening described as a ‘milestone that has been decades in the making’.

item.title: 'Yes Bibi or No Bibi': Netanyahu's political future overshadows Israel's election
item.description: Israel's upcoming legislative election could reshape the country's political future amid deep divisions over Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership. Former government spokesperson Eylon Levy tells Euronews what is at stake and why another war with Iran may be imminent.

item.title: Lula’s comeback puts brakes on Latin America’s rightward surge
item.description: Brazil’s re-elected leader now faces a hostile Congress at home and a Trump administration that had bet heavily on his rival.

item.title: Temu falls into line as EU backs its action plan after €200m fine
item.description: The Chinese-owned online retailer has promised stronger action to address several violations of the EU’s Digital Services Act, the European Commission said on Monday, following a €200 million fine in May.

item.title: The architectural heritage of Greece's Kea island: Vibrant colours, stone houses and watermills
item.description: Kea has around 2,500 permanent residents, and despite the growth of tourism, the island has managed to retain its traditional character.
